transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder.
Israel has bombed one of Gaza's biggest hospitals.
The Health Ministry says the overnight attack killed six people, including a Palestinian surgeon.
Empiraziah Batrawi reports that Israel's attacked Gaza throughout more than a year of ceasefire, killing more than 1,600 Palestinians.
Throughout the war, the Israeli military attacked Nasser Hospital, located in Hanyunas, killing patients and journalists.
But this latest overnight attack caught staff and patients by surprise because it came without warning during an agreed-upon ceasefire.
The Israeli airstrike hit the surgical ward, damaging also its intensive care unit.
Israel's military confirmed the attack, saying it targeted a senior Hamas figure, whom it did not name.
It said Hamas uses the hospital to store weapons and carry out interrogations.
Gaza's Health Ministry says a surgeon and other medical staff were killed in the airstrike on the hospital.
Hamas called the attack a war crime and said Israel must allow international journalists into Gaza to assess the facts themselves.
Aya Batrawi, NPR News, Dubai.
Democrat Scott Colombe celebrating victory in the Mississippi Senate race.
There were times when I was tired and I felt like I couldn't keep going, but I kept the faith.
And that is another tradition of our state.
There are so many people that have faith in Mississippi at times where it seemed impossible.
Colombe spoke to supporters gathered at Tougaloo College in Jackson Wednesday night after an Associated Press race call handed Colombe the win.
He narrowly defeated Cindy Hyde-Smith and is now set to become the first black Mississippi senator since Reconstruction.
Earlier this year, a joint investigation by Public Radio's Texas and California newsrooms revealed that the Trump administration is detaining unaccompanied migrant girls who are pregnant
in an area of Texas that lacks a specialized obstetric care they need.
That investigation led dozens of Democratic Congress members to question the policy.
Now they say the administration is not giving them straight answers.
Here's Mark Bettencourt reporting.
In a September letter responding to the Congress members' concerns,
Assistant Health Secretary Alex J. Adams wrote,
"There is no 'one size fits all' approach to the detention of pregnant unaccompanied minors,
but the government's own records, as well as interviews with multiple officials,
show the administration is intentionally placing pregnant girls in an area of South Texas that lacks specialized care,
and that roughly one in five of them has had to be transferred out of the state to get it."
Texas Congressman Joaquin Castro.
Obviously they're not being honest about their policy.
The administration did not respond to that allegation,
but said it takes steps to make sure the pregnant girls receive the care they need.
For NPR News, I'm Mark Bettencourt.
Texas Democrats say they're open to working with Elon Musk.
Musk poured millions of dollars into Republican races in the state,
as Michael Atkinson of Houston Public Media reports.
Musk had grown close to Texas Republicans like Governor Greg Abbott,
who advocated for tax breaks and public investments.
He spent more than $200 million on them this election cycle.
Now, Texas Democrats say they're open to working with Musk, with some stipulations.
Here's Governor-elect Gina Inajosa speaking on CNN.
We can have a strong working relationship with Elon Musk and his companies,
but it has to be on our terms.
It cannot be just running over the people of Texas.
And that's what changes now that I will be governor.
Musk said on social media that SpaceX and Tesla prospered in Texas, quote,
"because we were not constantly operating under an oppressive and extractive state government."
For NPR News, I'm Michael Atkinson in Houston.
Pope Leo has returned to Peru, where he served as a missionary for some 20 years.
A huge crowd waving balloons and flags greeted Leo as he arrived in Lima and declared Peru his homeland.
Leo's visit is the final leg of a three-nation South America.

Democrat Scott Colombe wins Mississippi Senate race, set to be first Black senator from the state since Reconstruction
